To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of scene classification is improved by (i) weighting of visual words, (ii) removal of visual words, and (iii) dimensionality reduction.

(1) the number of visual words is a crucial parameter that affects the classification performance, (2) the performance is sensitive to the choice of weighting scheme, and (3) the performance is improved by using a subset of visual words that are most discriminative.

the performance of scene classification using bag-of-words representations depends on the dimension, selection and weighting of visual-words, and that a combination of techniques from text categorization, such as term weighting and feature selection, is effective in improving the representation."

the following questions: How do different term weighting schemes affect the classification performance?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of the bag-of-visual-word representation depends on the type of image data.
, for scene classification, the bag of visual words representation performs well, but it is not a silver bullet.
the best performance is obtained by using a small number of features (e.g. 500) and by weighting features by tf-idf (term frequency-inverse document frequency) or by chi-squared statistic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best visual-word representations are obtained by: (1) selecting the most discriminative visual words, (2) removing stop-words, and (3) using the tf-idf weighting scheme.
a simple representation, with a small number of features and without weighting, is sufficient to produce a classification performance that is close to the state of the art.
The main takeaway from our work is that
visual words should be weighted based on their discriminative power and that feature selection is important.
, for scene classification, a visual-word representation with a large dimension and high weighting of visual words performs better than one with a small dimension and low weighting of visual words.
the choice of visual word representation can have a significant impact on the scene classification performance.
